One branch of a hyperbola (shown above) is defined by the parametric equations

$$
x=4\operatorname{tan}⁡t,\,y=3\operatorname{sec}⁡t.
$$

What is the domain of the parameter $t?$

feedback.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14062908/assets/82bdf962acd0e4a9beb29c7f3cc4930e66e6e56f41f81ba944fd470edfdb2cd8.png)

The quarter-hyperbola above is defined by the parametric equations

$$
x=\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{tan}⁡t,\,y=\sqrt{7}\operatorname{sec}⁡t.
$$

What is the domain of the parameter $t?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The parametric equations of the full hyperbola are

$$
x=\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{tan}⁡t,\,y=\sqrt{7}\operatorname{sec}⁡t,\,t\in [-\pi ,\pi ],\,t\ne \pm \frac{\pi }{2}.
$$

To restrict the parameterization to a quarter-hyperbola, we refer to the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14062908/assets/ec38ac9d02fbc8ec8c4f79fccb36a0e91833e852127fd1a8c84e492276b8f95d.png)

We can see that if we restrict $t$ to $[-\pi ,-\frac{\pi }{2})$ we get the required quarter-hyperbola.

Therefore, the parametric equations that describe the required quarter-hyperbola are

$$
x=\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{tan}⁡t,\,y=\sqrt{7}\operatorname{sec}⁡t,\,t\in [-\pi ,-\frac{\pi }{2}).
$$
